note.text:
In any triangle ABC, each side is shorter than the sum of the other two sides: AB < AC + CB. Going from A to B straight is shorter than going through C.
To test three lengths, check that the longest one is less than the sum of the other two. 4 cm, 5 cm, 7 cm: 7 < 4 + 5, so these make a triangle. 3 cm, 4 cm, 8 cm: 8 > 3 + 4, so they do not.
If the longest side equals the sum of the other two, the three points are on one straight line: AB = AC + CB means C is on the segment [AB].
If two sides are 5 cm and 8 cm, the third side is more than 8 − 5 = 3 cm and less than 8 + 5 = 13 cm.

worked_example.problem: Two sides of a triangle are {a} cm and {b} cm. The third side is a whole number of centimetres. What are its smallest and largest possible lengths?
steps: The third side must be less than the sum: less than {a} + {b} = {a + b} cm, so at most {a + b - one} cm.
The longest side {b} cm must be less than the other two together: the third side must be more than {b} − {a} = {b - a} cm, so at least {b - a + one} cm.
worked_example.answer: From {b - a + one} cm to {a + b - one} cm.
checks: triangleOk(a, b, a + b - one) && triangleOk(a, b, b - a + one) && !triangleOk(a, b, a + b) && !triangleOk(a, b, b - a)

cards.idea: In a triangle, the straight path is the shortest: each side is shorter than the other two sides put together.
example: Triangle ABC with AB = {ab} cm, AC = {ac} cm, CB = {cb} cm.
Through C: {ac} + {cb} = {ac + cb} cm, which is more than AB = {ab} cm.

check.prompt: Which statement is true for every triangle ABC?

wrong.explain: The straight side AB is the shortest way from A to B, so it is less than AC + CB.
That only happens when C is on the segment [AB]: then there is no triangle.
The straight side BC is shorter than going through A: BC < BA + AC.
That only happens when B is on the segment [AC]: then there is no triangle.

cards.idea: Three lengths make a triangle only if the longest one is less than the sum of the other two.
example: {a} cm, {b} cm, {c} cm: {c} < {a} + {b} = {a + b}, so they make a triangle.
{d} cm, {e} cm, {f} cm: {f} > {d} + {e} = {d + e}, so they do not.

cards.idea: If the longest length equals the sum of the other two, the three points are on one straight line.
example: AC = {a} cm, CB = {b} cm, AB = {a + b} cm: AC + CB = AB.
So C is on the segment [AB], and there is no triangle.

check.prompt: Points A, B and C have AC = {a} cm, CB = {b} cm and AB = {a + b} cm. What can you say?

misconceptions.explain: AC + CB is equal to AB, not more than AB, so there is no triangle: C is on [AB].
C is on [AB], but AC = {a} cm and CB = {b} cm are not equal, so it is not the midpoint.
If C were off the line, AC + CB would be more than AB. Here AC + CB = AB.

solution: The path through C is as short as the straight path, so {answer}.

cards.idea: The third side of a triangle is more than the difference of the other two sides and less than their sum.
example: Sides {a} cm and {b} cm: the third side is more than {b} − {a} = {b - a} cm and less than {b} + {a} = {a + b} cm.

check.prompt: Two sides of a triangle are {a} cm and {b} cm. Which length can the third side be?

misconceptions.explain: With {a + b} cm, the three points would be on one line: the third side must be less than {a + b} cm.
{a + b + k} cm is more than {a} + {b} = {a + b} cm, which is too long.
With {b - a} cm, the three points would be on one line: the third side must be more than {b - a} cm.
{b - a - 1} cm is less than {b} − {a} = {b - a} cm, which is too short.

solution: The third side must be more than {b} − {a} = {b - a} cm and less than {b} + {a} = {a + b} cm.

questions.prompt: Can {a} cm, {b} cm and {c} cm be the lengths of the sides of a triangle?

misconceptions.explain: The longest length is {max(a, max(b, c))} cm and the other two add up to {a + b + c - max(a, max(b, c))} cm. {triangleOk(a, b, c) ? 'The longest is less than the sum of the other two' : 'The longest is not less than the sum of the other two'}.

solution: The longest length is {max(a, max(b, c))} cm and the other two add up to {a + b + c - max(a, max(b, c))} cm.
{triangleOk(a, b, c) ? 'The longest is less than the sum of the other two' : 'The longest is not less than the sum of the other two'}, so the answer is {answer}.

questions.prompt: Two sides of a triangle are {a} cm and {b} cm. The third side is a whole number of centimetres. What is the longest it can be?

misconceptions.explain: With {a + b} cm, the three points are on one line: the side must be less than {a + b} cm.

solution: The third side must be less than {a} + {b} = {a + b} cm.
The largest whole number less than {a + b} is {answer}.

questions.prompt: Two sides of a triangle are {a} cm and {b} cm. The third side is a whole number of centimetres. What is the shortest it can be?

misconceptions.explain: With {b - a} cm, the three points are on one line: the side must be more than {b - a} cm.
The third side must be more than {b} − {a} = {b - a} cm.

solution: The third side must be more than {b} − {a} = {b - a} cm.
The smallest whole number more than {b - a} is {answer}.

questions.prompt: Two sides of a triangle are {a} cm and {b} cm. How many different whole-number lengths can the third side have?

misconceptions.explain: {b - a} cm and {a + b} cm are not allowed: the points would be on one line.
Counting from {b - a + 1} to {a + b - 1}, add one: there are {2 * a - 1} lengths.

solution: The third side is more than {b} − {a} = {b - a} cm and less than {a + b} cm.
So it can be any whole number from {b - a + 1} to {a + b - 1}.
